note: IP-neutral (issue #51). Issue #722: a broken droid in the desert is fixed with the plasma welder (hold E for its weld_s), no longer by waiting beside it; lines weld_wreck / weld_droid name what is welded. Companion droids: three kinds, each with look variants. Not LLM characters; they only beep. The player runs up to max_owned at once. They show in the inventory as droids; what a cargo droid carries does not show, and the Remnant never searches it. Prices: the merchant sells at price and buys back at resale. Looks: each kind's 'look' names its Hyper3D model (issue #25, content/look/gear_models.json), tinted by the variant's body colour ('tint' 0..1), with glowing 'eyes' and a 'muzzle' in model space (metres, facing -Z, standing on y = 0). No model = the droid_kit.gd primitives. Following (issue #25 follow-up): a droid stays put until the player is 'leash' metres away, then walks to its slot and stops within 'settle'.

rave.note: Issue #392: the moon rave's laser droid's colours: the stage's own (RaveDroid) and yours once it wears the laser rig (upgrades 'lasers').

raise.note: Issue #722: aiming, the arm raised straight out from the shoulder (DroidArmRaise directions in the droid's space, facing -Z).

bone_local_raised.note: Issue #722: the pistol with the arm raised out in front (DroidArmRaise, while it stands and fights): level, the barrel straight ahead. Solved about its own origin in the same bone frame.

club_vendor.label: Droid Merchant
club_vendor.note: Issue #392: the moon rave's droid merchant, at a stall of its own in the dome (town_kit.json 'club_dome' 'droid_vendor', on a planet whose 'club_dome' has 'droid_merchant'). Sells floating droids and the upgrades 'sold_at' 'rave' (the laser rig), and buys droids back like the market's.

lasers.label: Laser rig
lasers.modes_note: The rig has two settings, each a button on the droid's row in the Ledger (I): Lasers on or off, and Music, which steps through 'modes' in turn: the desert cantina mix, the moon rave mix, off ('music' a club playlist, content/look/sound.json; '' for the off station; 'label' what the button says). The music does not wait for the lasers. The droid plays its station on the club layer (Sound.set_droid), unmuffled, full within 'music.full_m' metres of you and fading out by 'hear_m'; the score ducks under it like a cantina's. A cantina you are inside and the ship's radio play over it. It stops while the droid is knocked out or waiting while you fly. Saved with the droid ('lasers_on', 'laser_music'); an older save kept one setting for both, so lasers on plays its 'laser_mode' and lasers off plays nothing. E beside the droid is its safety, as for any armed droid. Buying the rig shows the tip labels.lasers_tip.
lasers.note: Issue #392: the laser rig, for a floating droid ('kinds'), sold only by a droid merchant whose stall says it sells 'rave' upgrades (droids.json 'club_vendor'; 'sold_at'). Fitted, the droid wears the 'variant' look (black, magenta trim and eye) and a neon ring round its belly ('ring', model metres), and a fan of lasers hangs under it like the stage's laser droid ('fan': beams in two tiers dipping 'tiers' under level, 'spread' radians either side of ahead, 'length' metres (issue #703: 6, so from its 1.7 m hover the lowest beam ends half a metre over the floor and they no longer reach through walls and floors across the room; a fixed length, no ray per beam), sweeping 'sweep_deg' every 'sweep_s' seconds). A new rig is dark and quiet: its Lasers and Music buttons are in the Ledger (I), anywhere ('modes_note'). They go dark when it is knocked out and come back when it reboots.

upgrades.note: The droid merchant's upgrades, per droid (DroidRoster.upgrade). Each has one level per price: one level each now, the old three in one go at their old total (a save's droid with a level of an upgrade has all of it, DroidRoster.level). health: +per_level of the kind's 'hp' each level (every kind). cargo: +per_level hold slots each level on a droid that carries (a cargo droid starts with its kind's 'cargo_slots'; a slot is one kind of item, any number of it). damage: +per_level of its gun's damage each level (a droid with a gun). Your droids look their kind's 'base_variant' until their first upgrade of any kind, then its 'upgraded_variant' (a polished one: its 'shine' makes the model all-over metal with a clear coat, DroidKit). Your droids take hits from anyone you are fighting; at 0 hp one is knocked out for knocked_out_s, then reboots at full health.

engage_note: Assassin and floating droids of yours ('engage' on their kind): when one sees an enemy (enemies()) it walks up to 'advance' metres (about ten steps) toward it from where it stood, stopping 'standoff' metres short, and shoots from there. Once that enemy is dead (and no other is in sight) it comes back to you. Walk off far enough and it jumps to you as it always did.

taming.note: Block or deflect this many of the range remote's bolts in a row (a bolt that hits you resets the count) and it follows you home. Oda drops the hint as a rumor (rumors/port_town.json, r_remote_tame).

wrecks.note: Broken droids stranded in the desert. On the home planet's ball the first visit seeds ball_starting_count wrecks across the whole sphere, then every check_seconds of play, with this chance, one more turns up until ball_max_out. They stay at least ball_min_radius from town and ball_min_separation apart along the surface. The ball picks the kind with the fewest wrecks out, so all three are always in the field. Flat worlds keep max_out and the ring radii. An outpost cargo droid that runs off (issue #76) breaks down where it stops and is not part of the field: it is there to find until the world is built again, then gone. Fixing one takes fix_seconds; it resets and follows you.

pit_hauler.note: Issue #64: an old cargo droid that rattles round the landing pit, like T-89 a fixture of the pit. Nobody owns it. It carries the pickup named by 'carries' (pickups/port_town.json, pit_jetpack) on its back until someone takes it ([E] beside it, the same pickup as before, so saves still know it is taken). route: pit floor points (town coordinates) it walks in turn, stopping pause_s at each. Oda knows it as a rumor (rumors/port_town.json, r_pit_hauler).

station.note: The moon station (AsteroidWorld) has no street patrol under its dome: the home port's route crossed its walls and walked the hallway's roof. The town's droids (the side's 'units', cycled) pace short beats on the rock outside the ring wall instead, one at each angle in posts_deg (0 points down the hallway, so keep clear of it), 'out' metres beyond the wall, 'half' metres either way along it. Beats this far apart never overlap.

locals.note: Issue #187: the locals' white assassin droids. One walks each outpost the locals hold (its 'patrol' route), and once they hold the barracks two walk the Remnant's old main street patrol (remnant.patrol). They leave you alone until you hurt a local (their side's alarm) or shoot one, then fight like the Remnant's. Not for sale: the merchant's variants are player_variants.

remnant.note: Issue #64/#76: outpost_units are the droids each desert outpost keeps, each walking the outpost's point list named by 'route': an assassin droid on 'patrol', an armed floating droid on 'floater', and a cargo droid on 'cargo' ('walk_speed' sets its own pace). 'flee': when its outpost's alarm goes up (or it is shot) it runs 'distance' metres into the desert, away from you, at 'speed' (giving up after 'max_s'), and is left there broken: a wreck you can fix and keep. A new one turns up at the outpost when the troopers come back. The Remnant's own droids: they patrol the main street ('patrol': out along the street round the north rim of the landing pit and back the same way, never across the pit floor, which is T-89's), share the Remnant's standing (they turn on you when the garrison would), sound the town alarm when they see trouble, and fight. Killing one costs Remnant standing like a trooper.

wreck.belt_note: Issue #317: the three wrecks adrift in the belt under the ring station (stations/orbital_station.json 'belt') are sites too, with the same crews as the desert's, and extra_units of their own on top: droids on the spine routes (along the top of the hull, in its 'hull' frame, so they ride a wreck's dive and list with it), so every wreck you drop onto is a fight. Deeper is harder: two on the first, four on the second, six on the third, ending in two heavier assassins at the far end of the line.
wreck.sites_note: Wreck field: every wreck in 'sites' gets the same units on the same routes ('landmark' is the original's, which alone keeps the hauler and its red saber). skip_routes: routes over a deck that wreck lost (its 'variant') or that the sand has buried (_3 lies sunk past its middle: its hold floor and the gallery are under the sand), left unmanned. The 'level' routes are in the interior's design coordinates, the same on every wreck whatever its pose. A destroyed unit comes back after respawn_s (3 minutes) or as soon as you are respawn_away_m (500 ft) from where it fell, whichever is first. Units more than idle_beyond_m from you stand still on their route (nobody sees them walk) so four crews cost little.
wreck.zombie_note: Zombie droids: nobody deactivated the wreck crews and the sand has fried their circuits. They shoot anyone on sight whatever your standing, and scrapping one moves no faction's standing and starts no gossip. false puts them back under the Remnant (-6 Remnant standing per kill, like a town patrol droid).
wreck.note: Issue #148: what is left of the Remnant aboard the crashed starcruiser (src/systems/world/starcruiser_wreck.gd). routes: patrol points in one of the wreck's frames ('level': x, height v, stern-ward w, unpitched; 'hull': the pitched ship's own parts() frame), turned into world points by StarcruiserWreck.site_point. units walk their route and shoot on sight; they answer to no garrison, so nothing out there sounds the town's alarm. A destroyed one comes back on its route after respawn_s. Wreck cleanup: four assassins hold the bridge platform (its landing pad), floating droids drift on every tier, along the gallery and over the hold floor. hauler: an old cargo droid on the starboard deck with the pickup named by 'carries' (pickups/port_town.json, wreck_red_saber) on its back, like the pit hauler.

safety.note: Your droids' safety: with it on, an assassin or floating droid of yours shoots nobody, whatever happens. E beside one toggles it; the weapon wheel's slot 9 (and key 9) toggles all of them (on if any is off, else all off). eye_safe and eye_armed are its eyes' colour either way. A new droid's safety is off. A droid with the laser rig too: its lasers and music are buttons in the Ledger (I).
